reason: The text portrays the Hebrews as oppressed and suffering rather than ungrateful. They cry out to God in their distress (וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ), demonstrating dependence on and appeal to Yahweh. When they fail to listen to Moses (וְלֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה), the text explicitly attributes this to their condition—'from shortness of spirit and hard labor' (מִקֹּ֣צֶר ר֔וּחַ וּמֵעֲבֹדָ֖ה קָשָֽׁה)—not to ingratitude. Rather, they are too distressed and exhausted to receive the message. God responds positively to their cry, remembering his covenant, indicating approval of their plea rather than condemnation of ingratitude.
